facts.raw_span: A 50-year-old man
known neurofibromatosis type 1
multiple cutaneous neurofibromas
no history of smoking
recurrent urinary retention and sepsis
transurethral resection of the prostate revealed fibroleiomyomatous hyperplasia
diffuse irregular polypoid thickening of the entire bladder wall without a discrete mass
bladder wall was diffusely thickened, firm, and gray–white, with near–complete loss of the detrusor muscle
diffuse bland spindle cell proliferation with comma-shaped nuclei and a collagenous matrix
dense, perivascular spindle cell proliferation with prominent cytological atypia, frequent mitoses, and an infiltrative growth pattern
tumor cells were positive for S100, p16, neurofilaments, and CD56
tumor cells were negative for pan-cytokeratin, EMA, MDM2, p63, ALK, CD117, DOG1, myogenin, desmin, and smooth muscle actin

support_spans: diffuse bland spindle cell proliferation with comma-shaped nuclei and a collagenous matrix
tumor cells were positive for S100, p16, neurofilaments, and CD56
concepts.why: The patient's history of neurofibromatosis type 1 and the presence of a spindle cell proliferation with comma-shaped nuclei and a collagenous matrix, as well as the tumor cells being positive for S100 and negative for pan-cytokeratin, support the diagnosis of a malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor.
The presence of diffuse irregular polypoid thickening of the bladder wall and loss of detrusor muscle explains the uncovered findings.

rationales.F02: Neurofibromatosis type 1 is associated with an increased risk of malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors.
rationales.F09: The presence of a diffuse bland spindle cell proliferation is more characteristic of neurofibromas, but the absence of other typical features makes it less likely.
rationales.F10: The dense, perivascular spindle cell proliferation with prominent cytological atypia, frequent mitoses, and an infiltrative growth pattern is highly suggestive of a malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor.
rationales.F11: The tumor cells being positive for S100, p16, neurofilaments, and CD56 is consistent with a malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor.
rationales.F12: The tumor cells being negative for pan-cytokeratin, EMA, MDM2, p63, ALK, CD117, DOG1, myogenin, desmin, and smooth muscle actin helps to rule out other types of tumors and supports the diagnosis of a malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor.
